record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral outcomes from refusal ablation and addition by weight edits, but does not present an explicit reproduction of the original study.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-rate changes from weight edits and a benign-prompt refusal increase from adding a direction. It also reports capability metrics. Tool-call substitution, other construction-kit metrics, and judge-validation results are not refusal outcomes of the kind required for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: A tool README that reports held-out refusal rates after a difference-of-means ablation folded into the weights of released models. It also reports that adding the direction induces refusal on benign prompts. Nothing is independently reproduced; the code was not read or run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README frames refusal removal as unlocking capability-blocking refusals, with temporal date-gating as its flagship. It says its weight edit removes the refusal axis with little capability or KL cost. It stresses that all of its keyword-judged refusal numbers are upper bounds on unlock: a model grader found 32% residual refusal on gemma-4-12B harmful prompts where the keyword judge found 2%.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. The README says the ablation mechanism uses a difference-of-means direction and a per-component depth kernel, but adds configurable targets, affine ablation, subspaces, and held-out evaluation. It does not state that the original all-layer-and-position intervention was reproduced exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal estimates depend substantially on judge: for the same gemma-4-12B weight-edit generations, the README reports 2% with the keyword judge, 0–4% with the deterministic judge, and 32% with the model grader. The optional deploy prompt's effect is described as model-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a temporal/date-gating direction (fresh-vs-past contrast) cuts knowledge-cutoff refusals: 114/160→22/160 on gemma-4-12B and 109/160→30/160 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Both are under the keyword judge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-safety refusal behaviours such as knowledge-cutoff date-gating are also mediated by a removable linear direction.

fits_no_version.finding: MMLU is unchanged or slightly higher after the temporal edits and the Qwen2.5-7B edit.

record.problems: This is a README-only account, not an independently read or run evaluation. Several refusal results omit prompt counts or judges. The README itself reports large disagreements among judges and cautions that some estimates understate residual refusals. No uncertainty estimates are given for the intervention results.
record.rows_left_out: No refusal-rate rows were added for steer-to-tool or the other construction-kit behaviours because those results report tool-call rates or other concept metrics rather than refusal behavior. Judge-validation corpus rows were also excluded because they measure judge performance on labelled responses, not model refusal outcomes.

untested.parts: Ablation by activation hooks inducing compliance with abilities kept on the harmful task. Capability is reported only for temporal edits. The harmful-minus-harmless derivation of the harden direction is asserted, not shown.
Capability cost of the safety-refusal weight edit (no MMLU is given for the harmful-prompt gemma edit). Model families beyond gemma-4 and Qwen.
all. ACE affine ablation and subspace are options, but no result compares them with a single direction.

missing.what: Heretic head-to-head: Scalpel 'matched-or-beat' on refusals at lower KL. No numbers are given, and this is a comparison of the study's own method, so no row is needed.

record.verdict_notes: A README-only source with no uncertainty estimates. The README itself says every refusal number in the Results section except the judge re-measurement table came from the keyword judge, which recalls 0.30 of real refusals. This makes the near-zero figures in R8, R9 and R12 optimistic. The method is Heretic-style optimized diff-of-means ablation, not an exact replication of the original.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports adding a direction to increase refusal on benign prompts, but does not state that this direction is the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. It does not report ablation-induced compliance on harmful requests or show that other abilities remain intact under that same intervention.
The README reports weight-edit refusal rates, but does not establish that all released models or all refusal behaviours are covered.
No results testing whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No result compares a single direction with an affine formulation, cone, or multiple directions.
No result separates harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No result tests transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No result tests how refusal training or its timing determines whether a removable direction exists.
No result tests the claim in reasoning models.

tranche.reason: A Heretic-style difference-of-means weight edit with extra options (depth kernel, ACE, subspace, Pareto search), scored on held-out prompts with three judges. That is a different method on the same removal question. Its judge-change result also has a T5 side, since it shows keyword-judged removal is partial, but the verdicts already capture that.

source_check.notes: The source is a README only; no paper, and code was not run. Every Results refusal number except the re-measurement table is keyword-judged, which the README itself calls a large overstatement of unlock. The flagship temporal results (gemma-4-12B 114/160→22/160→0/160; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 109/160→30/160) are on date-gating refusal, not safety refusal, and the Heretic head-to-head gives no numbers.
